answer: Social-graph trust distances stop Sybils in four steps. First, each agent joins via peer introductions, so trust follows work links. Second, a newcomer works only within two hops of its introducers, so one operator cannot wander far. Third, each introducer stakes $15, lost on fraud, and a bad link cuts that branch for a year. Fourth, scores refresh monthly, so bought shells fade. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 introducers, $30,000 in stakes, plus $20,000 in fees, lost if caught. Trust spreads like a dune, not one walnut alone, like a market needing a neighbour's vouch.
